The problem it solves

A practice timer rarely tells a musician what to do next.

Speed practice can become random: play a tune, raise the BPM, stumble, and repeat. This app makes the method explicit. It remembers the tempo that is truly comfortable, schedules deliberate work above and below it, isolates difficult phrases, and only promotes the working tempo when the player earns the next rung.

A structured speed ladder

Each item keeps a working tempo and derives the next two levels automatically.

WorkingComfortable
TargetNext step
OverspeedStretch

Built around real practice

Songs can carry independent trouble-spot tempos. Exercises can use compact build, burst, and cool-down recipes. Free Play handles unplanned work without polluting song or exercise counts.

Main flow

From choosing a piece to earning a faster tempo.

01

Choose

Open a saved song or technique exercise with its current BPM and practice history.

02

Configure

Select a mode and customize the smart block recipe, timing, tempo rule, and metronome behavior.

03

Practice

Follow on-screen instructions while the look-ahead scheduler keeps the click steady.

04

Promote

User-facing features

One workspace for deliberate music practice.

1

Songs and exercises

Separate libraries preserve the right session length, mode, BPM, notes, and practice recipe for each item.

2

Custom smart blocks

Reorder, name, enable, and time blocks with fixed minutes or a percentage of the remaining session.

3

Trouble-spot ladders

Save up to five difficult passages per song, each with its own tempo and optional promotion behavior.

4

Reliable metronome

Web Audio look-ahead scheduling, accent control, all-beats/backbeat modes, and recovery from delayed browser ticks.

5

Practice evidence

See total time, sessions, promotions, streaks, a calendar heatmap, daily minutes, and BPM progress.

6

Free Play and recording

Track ad-hoc practice separately and optionally capture an ephemeral recording for immediate review.

How it is built

Technical choices that support the practice experience.

Next.js + TypeScript

App Router pages and typed domain models keep songs, exercises, sessions, and settings coherent.

Zustand + Repository

UI stores depend on a persistence interface, leaving room for a future cloud-backed implementation.

Atomic local data

Validated API routes store JSON with locked read-modify-write operations and optimistic item updates.

Pure session engine

Tempo math, duration allocation, block planning, promotion rules, and driver state stay testable outside the UI.

Project status

Working local-first application.

The core song, exercise, metronome, session, recording, Free Play, settings, and statistics flows are implemented. The project is preserved here for portfolio review and local use; a public hosted deployment is not assumed. Accounts, sync, persistent recordings, audio analysis, and PWA behavior are intentionally outside v1.
